eligibility.quote: Requested time 1691424773.212782 but the latest data is at time 3617.600000, when looking up transform from frame [map] to frame [odom]
eligibility.reason: E1/E4: a concrete navigation attempt fails on an incompatible time base. E2: the goal stamp crosses from the rviz plugin to the planner, rather than remaining an internal value. The source-code correction changes timestamp production, not just deployment names. E3: PAIR is supported as a data-flow composition, mediated by bt_navigator rather than a direct shared action endpoint.

failed_conditions.quote: Requested time 1691424773.212782 but the latest data is at time 3617.600000, when looking up transform from frame [map] to frame [odom]
failed_conditions.reason: The incompatible interpretation is the clock epoch of Header.stamp in a PoseStamped, not its nominal type or a seconds-versus-milliseconds conversion. representation_convention and the two listed elements fit that evidence.

supporting_evidence.quote: We're just making a clock willy-nilly which is going to default to system time.

loudness.quote: [planner_server-2] [WARN] [1691424774.006158189] [planner_server]: Could not transform the start or goal pose in the costmap frame
loudness.reason: Under S1's restricted definition this is silent_documented: the diagnostic occurs during navigation, not at build, connection, or component activation. It is not literally an absence of runtime errors.

detection_stage.quote: when I do Nav2Goal it throws the above provided error and robot do not move.
detection_stage.reason: The stack is already running; sending a navigation goal exposes the mismatch.

resolution.quote:
-  pose.header.stamp = rclcpp::Clock().now();
+  // pose.header.stamp = client_node_->now();  // client node doesn't respect sim time yet
resolution.reason: The published fix removes the system-clock stamp. The #3746 thread does not demonstrate the specification's exact mixed-revision composition working, so recommended rather than observed is justified.

notes: The concrete #3746 failure is established, but attribution to the exact installed 1.1.8 binary remains an inference: the report says ROS2 Humble Binary. The #3586 investigation and the inspected plugin code support the mechanism, not proof of that exact checkout. Later reports that rviz use_sim_time helped do not prove the separately constructed clock obeyed that parameter. The action inventory has a relay: navigate_to_pose and compute_path_to_pose are not one directly connected action pair.
